title: Khadga Dynasty
capsule: The Khadga dynasty ruled the Vanga and Samatata regions of ancient Bengal—broadly corresponding to present-day Bangladesh—from the mid-seventh to early eighth centuries CE, emerging after the collapse of Shashanka's Gauda kingdom. Five rulers are attested through copper-plate grants and coinage: Khadgodyama, Jatakhadga, Devakhadga, Rajabhatta, and Balabhatta, with the dynasty likely ending around 706–716 CE. The court was Buddhist in affiliation, and the copper-plate inscriptions record land grants to monasteries and Brahmin recipients. The Khadgas were succeeded by the Deva dynasty and ultimately by the Pala Empire, which unified Bengal from c. 750 CE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Dynastic succession and rough territorial extent are established from epigraphic sources (copper-plate grants), but precise geographic boundaries of Khadga control within the Bengal delta are not determinable from available evidence.
